title: Scalable Adaptation of 3D Geometric Foundation Models via Weak Supervision from Internet Video
claim: Limited labeled data bottlenecks 3D models; tapping abundant video through our framework yields better zero-shot results that keep improving with more data.
layout: Single collage: left-to-right pipeline metaphor, top baseline/ours renders, bottom-right three scaling plots
description: A busy collage built around a pipe metaphor. At upper left, a small blue bucket labeled 'Limited Labeled 3D Data (e.g., ScanNet, 1K scenes)' feeds a thin pipe. A red no-entry sign marks it as the 'Data Scarcity Bottleneck'. At lower left, wide streams of blue and gray video ribbons flow into a cylindrical 'SAGE Framework' tube. Inside the tube are a sparse graph, an orange cube and a green surface, with a green arrow labeled Sparse Geometry Anchors, Dense Spatiotemporal Consistency and Regularization Data. At upper right, two point-cloud renders of a living room are labeled 'Baseline' (noisy, fragmentary) and 'Ours' under the heading 'General-Purpose 3D Foundation Model (Zero-shot Generalization)'. At lower right, a gray panel titled 'Scalability' holds three log-log plots (MP3D, 7-Scenes, TUM) of Chamfer Distance falling as training scene count rises from 100 to 10,000, each with a dashed power-law fit.
caption: Overview of the SAGE framework for scaling a General-Purpose 3D Foundation Model. To overcome the Data Scarcity Bottleneck inherent in limited labeled 3D datasets, we propose a pipeline that leverages abundant static-scene Internet videos to achieve robust zero-shot generalization on complex unseen scenes. Bottom right: Scalability analysis demonstrates zero-shot reconstruction performance as training data scales from 100 to 10K video scenes, showing consistent improvement with increased data volume across various benchmarks (MP3D, 7-Scenes, and TUM).
abstract: Geometric foundation models show promise in 3D reconstruction. However, their progress is severely constrained by the scarcity of diverse, large-scale 3D annotations. While static-scene Internet videos are abundant and diverse, utilizing them as a scaling source for geometric learning is challenging due to the absence of ground-truth geometry and the presence of observational noise. To address this, we propose SAGE, a framework for Scalable Adaptation of GEometric foundation models from raw video streams. SAGE leverages a hierarchical mining pipeline to transform videos into training trajectories and hybrid supervisions: (1) Informative training trajectory selection; (2) Sparse Geometric Anchoring via SfM point clouds for global structural guidance; and (3) Dense Differentiable Consistency via 3D Gaussian rendering for multi-view constraints. Besides, we also introduce a regularization strategy that replays a small fraction of supervised data to prevent catastrophic forgetting. Applied to two architecturally distinct backbones, SAGE reduces Chamfer Distance on unseen benchmarks (7Scenes, TUM-RGBD, Matterport3D) by 20-42% with MV-DUSt3R and consistently improves VGGT. SAGE establishes Internet video as a viable and scalable adaptation source for geometric foundation models. Code is available at https://github.com/aim-uofa/SAGE.
